title: OpenAI-backed Thrive Holdings acquires ADT
content:
Thrive Holdings has acquired physical security company ADT for $10 per share or about $7.6 billion in equity, the companies announced on Thursday. Beyond equity, the total enterprise value of the deal is $15.3 billion, ADT said.
Thrive Holdings is the holding company spinout from Josh Kushner’s powerhouse VC firm Thrive Capital. It also counts OpenAI as its partner, as well as an investor. The firm’s mission is to hold other companies long-term, revitalizing them with AI. Currently, Thrive Holdings holds over 75 companies, it says.
As a partner, OpenAI supplies AI models and tech as well as people, otherwise known as forward-deployed engineers, to Thrive’s companies.
Neither ADT nor Thrive announced what new AI-powered security products they will be releasing, but they did tease that the plan was to invest and release new products. “ADT will form the foundation of Thrive Holdings’ smart home security business,” the press release said.
AI-powered physical security is having a moment right now. Apple just entered the field with a new line of smart home and home security products in collaboration with LG and Schneider Electric. Amazon updated its smart home line, including new AI-powered home cameras. ADT already partners with Apple and Google and is expected to continue to do so. And who knows what the future might bring? Some startups are offering AI dog robots as roving security guards.
Note: This story was updated to include ADT’s current partnerships and to describe Thrive Holdings as a holding company.

report.summary: OpenAI-backed Thrive Holdings is acquiring ADT for about $7.6 billion in equity, making the security giant the foundation of its AI-powered smart-home push.
report.background: Thrive Holdings is a long-term holding company spun out of Thrive Capital, with OpenAI as both partner and investor. Its strategy is to acquire established businesses and modernize them with AI models, engineering talent and product investment; it says it holds more than 75 companies. ADT is a legacy physical-security provider with broad residential and commercial reach and existing ties to Apple and Google. The deal arrives as big tech and startups race into AI-enabled home security: Apple has launched smart-home products with partners, Amazon refreshed AI cameras, and robotics startups are testing autonomous guards. Buying ADT gives Thrive distribution, installation and monitoring infrastructure that pure software AI companies lack.
key_points: Thrive Holdings agreed to pay $10 per ADT share, about $7.6 billion in equity; total enterprise value is $15.3 billion. ADT will become the foundation of Thrive's smart-home security business. The companies teased investment and new products but did not name specific AI features, pricing or launch dates.

OpenAI is not just an investor: it supplies models, technology and forward-deployed engineers to Thrive's portfolio companies. That arrangement could embed OpenAI models into ADT's cameras, sensors, monitoring workflows and customer support. It also gives OpenAI a channel into physical security, a market with sensitive data, regulatory scrutiny and high reliability requirements.

AI physical security is heating up. Apple entered smart home and home security with LG and Schneider Electric, Amazon updated AI-powered home cameras, and startups are pitching robot guards. ADT already works with Apple and Google and is expected to keep those ties, so Thrive must improve ADT without disrupting existing ecosystems.

Thrive's holding-company model aims to revitalize mature firms with AI rather than build from scratch. ADT brings installers, monitoring centers and millions of customers, but AI upgrades must handle false alarms, privacy, outages and liability. Integration and consumer trust will matter as much as model quality.
report.impact: For the AI industry, the deal signals that AI consolidation is moving into physical-world services, not just software. It validates a model where OpenAI partners with holding companies to inject models and engineers into legacy businesses. For developers, expect demand for edge AI, computer vision, video analytics, privacy-preserving ML and integrations with home platforms; OpenAI's involvement may create APIs and partner opportunities, but also platform lock-in concerns. For regular users, ADT could get smarter alerts, natural-language controls and automated monitoring, while raising questions about data collection, subscription pricing and whether AI reduces or adds false alarms. Regulators may scrutinize camera data and emergency-response reliability.
report.tools: To follow the space, watch Home Assistant and Frigate for local AI camera detection, Scrypted for bridging smart-home cameras into Apple and Google ecosystems, and OpenCV plus YOLO or TensorFlow Lite for edge vision prototypes. OpenAI's API and Realtime API are useful for natural-language security assistants. For privacy-first experiments, try local LLMs and on-device vision models. Also track ADT's developer and partner announcements and Apple HomeKit Secure Video, Google Nest and Amazon Alexa integrations.
